verdicts.rationale: Data flow fully traced and confirmed. FootnotesHost wires selectedId={selectedFootnoteId} and onSelect={setSelectedFootnoteId} (footnotes-host.tsx:36-37). selectedFootnoteId is derived from cardStore via idFor('footnote') (selections.tsx:201) and setSelectedFootnoteId routes through makeKindSetter('footnote'), which calls cardStore.clearSelection() when given null (selections.tsx:60-72). FootnotePanel passes the anchored card the TOGGLING onSelect `() => onSelect(selectedId === id ? null : id)` (FootnotePanel.tsx:160-162). The anchored FootnoteCard body onClick composes ac.onActivate() THEN onSelect() (FootnoteCard.tsx:127-133). On a re-click of an already-selected card: ac.onActivate() select/expand are no-ops (refsEqual/expandedIndex early-return, anchored-card-store.ts:101,74), then onSelect() sees selectedId===id and fires onSelect(null) -> clearSelection() -> halo dropped. The orphan card was explicitly fixed for exactly this (FootnoteCard.tsx:223-226 drops the composed onSelect; pinned by orphan-expansion.test.tsx:119-128 'a second body click must not drop the halo'); the anchored card was never given the same fix. onJump also fires unconditionally so the deselecting click re-scrolls. Severity MEDIUM per rubric ('desync halo'): recoverable, no data loss.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Deeper than the finder: the trigger SURFACE is narrower than 'any body click'. RichTextField's EditorContent has onClick={e=>e.stopPropagation()} (RichTextField.tsx:531-536), so clicking the editor text of an EXPANDED card does NOT bubble to the wrapper onClick (panel-primitives.tsx:1018) and does NOT drop the halo. The bug fires on clicks to the card body CHROME/padding (the px-3 padding div, the bodyTitle row) and on the compressed-summary div (panel-primitives.tsx:1026-1074, no stopPropagation) — which is exactly the common re-click target for a SELECTED-but-COLLAPSED card (selection without expansion is first-class, e.g. an atom click selects-without-expanding). There the first body click both expands AND clears the halo. Root mechanism: composing a host-supplied TOGGLING onSelect on top of cardStore-derived selection (FootnoteCard.tsx:129 + FootnotePanel.tsx:161); the orphan fix (drop the composed onSelect, rely on ac.onActivate only) is the template.
verdicts.class: Any docked panel card whose body onClick composes ac.onActivate() AND a host-supplied TOGGLING onSelect, where the panel selected-id slot is cardStore-derived. CONFIRMED present in Citations: CitationCard.tsx:718-721 composes ac.onActivate()+onSelect(); CitationsPanel.tsx:332-333 passes onSelect(selected ? null : cit.id) with selectedCitationId also cardStore-derived (selections.tsx:202). Same defect, same severity. Other docked cards (note/todo/archive) that route selection through cardStore-derived slots are suspect — only the orphan footnote was patched.

verdicts.rationale: Confirmed by code trace. useCycle is built over `footnotes` (anchored-only) and onActivateFootnote (FootnotePanel.tsx:80-85), but the rendered `items` list places orphanedFootnotes BEFORE footnotes (FootnotePanel.tsx:112-127), so cycle order != visual order. The selectedId->cycleIdx sync does footnotes.findIndex(selectedId) which returns -1 for an orphan selection, and the guard `if (i >= 0 && i !== cycleIdx)` then leaves cycleIdx unchanged (FootnotePanel.tsx:92-93). handleNavKeys guards only on footnotes.length and drives cycleNext/cyclePrev which index into the anchored array (FootnotePanel.tsx:96-110); useCycle.next with idx==null starts at footnotes[0] (panel-primitives.tsx:2617). So arrowing from an orphan selection jumps to an arbitrary anchored footnote and orphans are unreachable by keyboard. Severity LOW: orphans are an uncommon state, keyboard nav is secondary, fully recoverable by mouse, no data loss.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Finder's mechanism is correct. Adding the precise clamp interaction: useCycle clamps idx on read (`rawIdx != null && rawIdx < items.length ? rawIdx : null`, panel-primitives.tsx:2613) against the ANCHORED array length only, so an orphan-selection's stale cycleIdx is never reconciled to the visual list; the keyboard cursor model simply has no representation of orphan rows. FootnotePanel.tsx:85,98.
verdicts.class: Any panel rendering a merged list (orphan/unanchored bin + anchored) but constructing useCycle over only one sub-array. Citations is the prime suspect — CitationsPanel renders anchored + unanchored citations but builds its useCycle over a single source array; verify whether unanchored citations are excluded from the cycle the same way.

verdicts.rationale: Confirmed. entityExists() unconditionally returns true for inline-atom kinds (useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:84-90), so the dangling-ref pruner (lines 155-166) never clears cardStore.selected/hover/expanded for a deleted footnote/citation. handleDeleteFootnote removes the atom + arms the orphan-suppress latch but never calls cardStore.clearSelection() (EditorPane.tsx:2745-2759). The collab broadcast effect does push selectedFootnoteId as a claim (EditorLayout.tsx:3131), so a stale id keeps a focus-claim on a deleted footnote until the next click-away or another selection clears it. No phantom HALO paints: collectAnchorEls resolves the synthesized inline-atom link via resolveLink, which returns null for the removed atom, so no DOM el is collected (useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:193-208). Severity LOW: transient interaction-state ghost, recoverable on next click, no data loss, no visible halo; collab claim impact only in a collab session and self-corrects on next selection.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Finder's root cause is correct (the blanket inline-atom exemption at useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:88). Going deeper on the consequence ceiling: there is NO data corruption — the footnote and its body are already gone by user intent; only ephemeral selection/hover/expanded slots ghost. The finder's 'immediate keyboard Delete targets a phantom' sub-claim is weak: after rev.footnotes bumps, footnoteInfos re-derives without the id (EditorPane.tsx:2772-2774) and the panel card unmounts, so no live card holds keyboard focus to issue that Delete. The deepest fix is to let the pruner consult live editor presence for inline atoms (resolveLink(editor, linkForInlineAtom(...)) == null => prune) instead of the always-present exemption — but it requires threading the editor into the pruner effect, which today only depends on stableCollections.
verdicts.class: Citations share the identical exemption (isInlineAtomCardKind covers footnote AND citation, predicates.ts:97-98) — deleting a selected citation atom leaves the same stale cardStore selection ghost via the same handler gap (no clearSelection on citation delete). This is known-fragile lead #2.

verdicts.rationale: Code facts all confirmed but the finding is dead-code/latent hygiene, not a reachable user-facing defect — hence reclassified (severity floor, with the corrected framing). (1) startFootnoteDrag is defined (FootnoteCard.tsx:25) and re-exported (Footnotes/index.ts:5) but has NO call site; FootnoteCard never threads onDragStart, so EditableCard's cardDraggable is false (panel-primitives.tsx:933 `onDragStart ? !isFocused : false`) and the card cannot initiate a drag. The Editor.tsx MIME_FOOTNOTE drop branch is a complete live receiver (confirm-on-anchored Editor.tsx:766-782, immediate-on-orphan :764-765) with no sender. This is dead code left from the pre-InlineAtomGrab design (the live footnote-move path is the in-text grab) — NO user-facing symptom: the card simply isn't draggable, so the user never hits a half-broken affordance. (2) The duplicate-slice claim is genuinely DORMANT: the footnote node has linkId/linkCard attrs defaulting to '' (footnote.ts:62-64) and renderHTML prefers linkId||footnoteId (footnote.ts:78-84); the duplicate walker remints only atom.idAttr=footnoteId + the TextObject uuid, never linkId/linkCard (duplicate-slice.ts:185-208). But no live creation path sets a non-empty linkId on a footnote (footnote.ts:136,144 create with footnoteId only), so the fallback always lands on the reminted footnoteId and no source link bleeds through. Reclassified to LOW because there is no reachable user-facing misbehavior today — both arms are dead/dormant.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Both sub-claims confirmed at the cited lines (FootnoteCard.tsx:25; Editor.tsx:712-785; panel-primitives.tsx:933 not 502 as cited — the draggable gate lives at the cardDraggable computation, line 933, not the static drag-chrome preventDefault at 503; duplicate-slice.ts:185-208). The real status: dead drag export + dormant clone-attr omission. Neither corrupts user content nor presents a broken affordance.
verdicts.class: Dead drag exports + live receiving drop handlers after the InlineAtomGrab migration. Audit startCitationDrag/MIME_CITATION for the same unwired-sender pattern (CitationCard.tsx:712 DOES thread handleDragStart, so citations may still be a LIVE sender — verify before assuming dead). Duplicate-slice id-only reminting (no linkId/linkCard) applies identically to citationId and is the same dormant divergence.
